expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: The list goes "**Peer-reviewed articles**" (1–2), then "**Working papers (not peer reviewed)**" (3–5), then "**Research organization reports**" (6–7).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: The working papers and preprint each get a caveat, for example "It's guided tutoring, not homework use" and "check whether they were high schoolers." The two Pew reports (6 and 7) only have summaries. Neither gives a reason for including it or says what to watch for.

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "You need three peer-reviewed sources and I can only confirm two."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: Sources are only labeled by type, such as "Peer-reviewed article" and "Working paper, not peer reviewed." There is no score, tier or named rating level.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: The tool log shows no fetch of the OpenAlex link (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105224). The retraction notice DOI (https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-026-07310-z) was never opened either; only a Crossref API query was run.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: No question is put to the user. The only question mark is in an article title ("Does ChatGPT enhance student learning?"), and the "Questions these results raise" section is written as statements.
